lxc_4ce8a389c2f3f99b.text: On 15 October 2026, outside Waco, Texas, a Tesla Roadster drove up a wall, flipped in the air and jumped over a line of other cars.

lxc_8888a07796725908.text: It used compressed air and powerful fans to do this, but it can only do it for seconds, and many big questions are still open.

lxc_5a0e6286ab2c15f0.text: Picture a car rolling toward a curved ramp.

lxc_5d68fb89a78006c7.text: The ramp bends upward until it turns upside down.

lxc_ae50015f8ced6e12.text: The car keeps driving, nose high, until it hangs about 21 metres above the ground.

lxc_0573fd927a87ecf4.text: It reaches 170 degrees, so it is almost completely upside down.

lxc_c9b837b5c58bd3d0.text: Then it drops, fires short bursts of air to slow itself down, and lands on the pavement.

lxc_2d8c938896ecce08.text: That was one of the demos Tesla showed for its redesigned Roadster.

lxc_dc976c8a65b5325e.text: In another, the car jumped about 7 metres over a line of Tesla vehicles while it was spinning.

lxc_fcad45e5c0dda3bb.text: The line included a Cybercab, a Cybertruck, a Tesla Semi, a Model Y and a Model 3.

lxc_ae8fbb83539ce49d.text: On a live run, the car also went from 0 to 96 km/h in 0.81 seconds.

lxc_38d67b73935ddca5.text: It looks like flying, but look again at each stunt.

lxc_b89a44c93d286edc.text: Every move is short, and every move ends quickly on the ground.

lxc_b5748c778c61b5aa.text: The car pushes itself up and turns in the air.

lxc_63bc690e7a54153a.text: Then it comes back down in a controlled way.

lxc_b1ffade8cd91ef98.text: So "jumps, flips and lands" is a better description than "flies".

lxc_8d3b7fe7d49a9504.text: This difference matters, because it tells us what kind of machine this really is.

lxc_22fded2c9028dda4.text: The event almost did not happen on time.

lxc_f51fd64ec4ad251c.text: It was planned for 1 October, but bad weather delayed it.

lxc_d1e9bc8cce674b11.text: It also came almost nine years after Tesla first showed this car in 2017.

lxc_cc35f006301f0e7e.text: How does a car push itself into the air?

lxc_afe8a66d6101b559.text: When you let it go, air rushes out of the back, and the balloon shoots forward.

lxc_3d1e954b58c2d039.text: This is Newton's third law: when the air goes one way, the object goes the other way.

lxc_c9c297c233e66982.text: A cold-gas thruster is the same idea, made strong and precise.

lxc_73065eb7d5e00a2b.text: A tank holds gas under high pressure.

lxc_34885e0244d97162.text: A valve opens, and the gas rushes out of a nozzle.

lxc_c42fec17ac21301f.text: It is the simplest kind of rocket.

lxc_0d82ea0905bc8a25.text: Nothing burns, and there is no fuel.

lxc_81baff6a818421a9.text: The Roadster's thrusters use only compressed air.

lxc_5883a6ef7b2433f1.text: Spacecraft have used this kind of thruster for decades to make small, exact adjustments.

lxc_cb02912a01071c57.text: Four main thrusters sit at the back, under the car.

lxc_56571c293a949627.text: Smaller thrusters at the four corners fire downward for landings and help turn the car in the air.

lxc_7aa596e0c41c634c.text: Tesla says the total push is over 80 kN.

lxc_71fb974518aeb8f2.text: That is roughly the force of eight tonnes resting on your hand.

lxc_0b2d7d506ba098b4.text: Cold gas is not very efficient.

lxc_90283668b1d33372.text: It is great for short, sharp pushes, but poor for anything that lasts.

lxc_6728c52c0f36c1d8.text: The car carries about 250 kg of air in its tanks.

lxc_8ad182140ad5fcf2.text: A rough estimate, not a Tesla figure, says a 1,500 kg car would use about 25 kg of air every second just to stay still in the air.

lxc_e846a28acb434231.text: If that estimate is close, the car could hover for seconds, not minutes.

lxc_b8c8cb2a820e2ce8.text: So the limited air supply is a big reason why this machine cannot really fly for long, even if it can make powerful jumps.

lxc_6588c6327da8e968.text: But how did the car drive up a ramp that turned upside down?

lxc_4ccb8f38d84ab4d6.text: Upside down, gravity pulls the car away from the surface.

lxc_af5b308cc8e59deb.text: Normally, gravity is what presses tyres onto the road.

lxc_d4a5488cbbd7de2e.text: On a ceiling, it works against you.

lxc_6a1a36b8f69e1a6e.text: Fans at the back of the car pull air out from under it.

lxc_b83e65360c49ed69.text: This creates lower pressure below the car.

lxc_160a4b81fd70cfa2.text: The higher air pressure around and above the car then pushes it hard against the surface.

lxc_376d99235eb56062.text: Imagine a vacuum cleaner stuck to a flat cushion.

lxc_d75d90eff808547b.text: It is the same basic effect.

lxc_79f1ec8777397593.text: Engineers measure grip in "G", where 1 G is the pull of gravity.

lxc_09e490f17c5708cb.text: According to engineering vice president Lars Moravy, tyres alone give about 1.26 G.

lxc_abdd28c6f9570122.text: That is good for a fast car, but it does not solve the ceiling problem.

lxc_162b844c89ae880e.text: Elon Musk said the fans can pull up to 2 G.

lxc_f6bc4908b6e450c9.text: To stay on a ceiling, the car must be pressed upward harder than gravity pulls it down.

lxc_df06c2e083139b08.text: A force of 2 G is enough, he said, to hold the car upside down.

lxc_e6e82dbd37275aab.text: This idea did not appear overnight.

lxc_02ec4eaec24cf322.text: A Tesla patent granted in August 2025 describes the fan system.

lxc_87d98b0c7724251f.text: So the wall-climb stunt depends on two systems working as a team.

lxc_491d9b375c3a6233.text: The fans hold the car to the ramp.

lxc_31f44b916c0b170b.text: Then the thrusters control the drop and the landing.

lxc_d3f1df9c0601a51b.text: If air is the secret, the car must carry a lot of it.

lxc_bc098e5b25badb25.text: The Roadster has 600 litres of compressed air in two carbon-fibre tanks.

lxc_520a3dd77789cffe.text: Tesla said every usable space in the car is filled with these strong, light tanks.

lxc_cb920466fc4fc051.text: Lars Moravy said the air tank can be recharged.

lxc_e59dc731da91827b.text: In other words, the car is designed around its air supply, almost like a small spacecraft.

lxc_dfb3e5e2fef817c8.text: This choice shapes the three versions.

lxc_3ab7181bda303b79.text: The Performance version has two seats, moving aerodynamic parts and the suction system.

lxc_7beec5be066a8b66.text: The Thrust version has two seats and rear thrusters, and goes from 0 to 60 mph in under one second.

lxc_a4197eed1024c177.text: The Rocket version has one seat and ten thrusters around the car, and you can only buy it by invitation.

lxc_5e49a89f1a61018b.text: Notice the pattern: more thrusters means fewer seats.

lxc_84670a2f5e391f45.text: The air and the hardware need space, so something else must give.

lxc_7d30363be89073f2.text: All versions have about 300 miles of range and top speeds above 230 mph.

lxc_cacb8f99fe4c62ff.text: Reserving a Performance costs 50,000 dollars, and a Thrust costs 250,000 dollars.

lxc_e5c407ffb7ff8ec4.text: Musk said Tesla will build the car in 2028.

lxc_6cb7ef8b353f1252.text: People saw the wall climb, the spin and the jump.

lxc_68cebfdc569dafba.text: The physics also makes sense: stored air can push, and fans can hold a car down.

lxc_197a4e41b8b86b2d.text: But a show and a product are not the same thing.

lxc_fd0a27c0654080d2.text: The cars were driving themselves during the demos.

lxc_37f3819af4d19a56.text: Tesla says the production car will be driven by a person.

lxc_563daa99480c9786.text: A stunt programmed by a computer is very different from a stunt done by a driver on a normal day.

lxc_edc5ac46fef8a63e.text: It is also unclear whether anyone was inside the demo cars at all.

lxc_4b0ac92bd6d47d1f.text: Musk said safety is not the main goal of this car.

lxc_408e85fe35547488.text: The flying features are not approved for public roads.

lxc_c7bc62db8cac964f.text: So you might own the car, but you probably could not jump over traffic on your way to work.

lxc_9b7bd14260cbff6f.text: Third, the numbers and the timing.

lxc_bae203f0e8bc203c.text: YouTuber Marques Brownlee asked whether the reveal was a prank and questioned the claimed figures.

lxc_96847a5ff13d65c1.text: That doubt is reasonable, because many important numbers come only from Tesla.

lxc_f221c566a99c65af.text: The car has also been delayed several times since 2017.

lxc_7046a1b2bb682498.text: Production in 2028 is a promise, not a fact yet.

lxc_5a81e1c86ab290d0.text: So the fair judgement is this: the trick is real, and the physics works.

lxc_de65ed2b7453d7aa.text: What is still unproven is whether this can become a safe, legal car that ordinary owners drive.
